title: Finite compact-support Leray filtration in constructible Weil sheaves
statement:
Fix a finite field $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, its algebraic closure $k$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k_0)$ and an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $h:X_0\to Z_0$ and $g:Z_0\to Y_0$ be separated finite-type morphisms of $k_0$-schemes, with $Z_0,Y_0$ quasi-separated and of finite type over $k_0$. Use constructible $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-Weil sheaves, namely Frobenius-fixed pairs in the constructible heart of the common-stage coefficient category, as in [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex], and the compact-support functors of [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support], with $R^it_!\mathcal F=\mathcal H^i(Rt_!\mathcal F)$ on the geometric fibers, carrying their natural Weil structures. For every constructible Weil sheaf $\mathcal F$ on $X_0$ and every integer $n\geq0$, there is a finite filtration by constructible Weil subsheaves
$$
0=G_0\subseteq G_1\subseteq\cdots\subseteq G_m=R^n(gh)_!\mathcal F.
$$
For each $1\leq j\leq m$ there are integers $a_j,b_j\geq0$ with $a_j+b_j=n$, a constructible Weil sheaf $S_j$, a monomorphism
$$S_j\hookrightarrow R^{a_j}g_!\bigl(R^{b_j}h_!\mathcal F\bigr)$$
and an epimorphism
$$S_j\twoheadrightarrow G_j/G_{j-1}.$$
All filtration maps, monomorphisms and epimorphisms are morphisms of Weil sheaves. No mixedness or weight hypothesis is imposed on $\mathcal F$.

proof.text: Work in the underlying common-stage triangulated categories, not in a purported triangulated category of Weil pairs. Their constructible hearts are abelian by [def-weil-constructible-heart]. By [prop-constructible-truncations], geometric Frobenius pullback $Lg^*$ commutes with truncation and cohomology, so it preserves the heart. By [lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback] it is, on integral representatives, the termwise inverse image along the automorphism $g$, an exact functor of complexes with inverse the termwise inverse image along $g^{-1}$; rationalization and the common-stage prescription of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] keep this. Hence $Lg^*$ is an exact autoequivalence of the triangulated category commuting with shifts, and it restricts to an exact equivalence of each heart. The category of its fixed pairs is abelian as well: for an equivariant map take its kernel and cokernel in the underlying heart; applying the exact equivalence carries each to the kernel or cokernel of the pulled-back map, and their universal properties induce invertible Frobenius structures. The same universal properties give the induced maps. Thus kernels, cokernels and images are computed in the underlying heart, and exactness is detected there. These are precisely the constructible Weil sheaves of [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex].

source.place: First paragraph: spectral sequence of Weil sheaves; the abelian category used for all terms.

proof.text: Put $K=Rh_!\mathcal F$ and $T=Rg_!$ on the geometric fibers. Apply [lem-zl-field-shriek-lower-bound] to $h$ and $g$: $K$ is bounded constructible with $\mathcal H^b(K)=0$ for $b<0$, and $T$ is triangulated, preserves bounded constructibility, and preserves every lower cohomological bound. The finite-type and quasi-separated hypotheses hold for $X_0$ as well: finite type follows by composing $h$ with $Z_0\to\operatorname{Spec}k_0$, and quasi-separatedness follows by composing the separated map $h$ with the quasi-separated structure map of $Z_0$. These properties pass to geometric fibers. By [lem-fix-weil-operations], $K$ and its subsequent compact-support images carry their natural Weil structures. All constructions below take place in the underlying common-stage categories with these structures retained. Here finite-type composition and base change are [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change], separated finite-type base change is [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change], and quasi-separated source/base-change permanence is [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](2),(3); a separated morphism is quasi-separated because its diagonal is a closed immersion and hence quasi-compact.

source.place: First paragraph: K=Rh_!F is bounded constructible, and T=Rg_! is exact.

proof.text: For every integer $b$, let $K_b=\tau^{\le b}K$. The truncation properties in [prop-constructible-truncations] and [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles](1) identify the successive truncation triangle as $K_{b-1}\to K_b\to\mathcal H^b(K)[-b]\to K_{b-1}[1]$. Apply the triangulated functor $T$ from [lem-zl-field-shriek-lower-bound], then the cohomological functors of [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles](5). Define $D^{a,b}=\mathcal H^{a+b}(TK_b)$ and $E^{a,b}=\mathcal H^{a+b}(T(\mathcal H^b(K)[-b]))$. The inclusion maps, projection maps and boundary maps give respectively $\alpha:D^{a,b}\to D^{a-1,b+1}$, $g:D^{a,b}\to E^{a,b}$ and $f:E^{a,b}\to D^{a+2,b-1}$. The three consecutive portions of the long exact sequences give exactly the three image-kernel equalities of [def-sp-exact-couple]. This constructs a type-zero exact couple. Truncation and cohomology commute with Frobenius by [prop-constructible-truncations], so $K_b$, $\mathcal H^b(K)[-b]$ (with the shifted structure) inherit Weil structures. Since $Lg^*$ is triangulated (step 1), it carries the truncation triangle of $K$ to a triangle with terms in the same truncation ranges; by the uniqueness in [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles](1) it is the truncation triangle of $Lg^*K$, and the Weil structure of $K$ induces the unique isomorphism of triangles, so all three maps, including the boundary $\mathcal H^b(K)[-b]\to K_{b-1}[1]$, are maps of Weil complexes. Applying $T$ preserves this for the first two maps and for $T$ of the boundary by [lem-fix-weil-operations]; the shift comparison $T(K_{b-1}[1])\simeq(TK_{b-1})[1]$ used to form the image triangle is a map of Weil complexes by [lem-zl-weil-shriek-shift-compatibility]. Hence $\alpha$, $g$ and $f$ are equivariant. Exactness in the Weil heart follows from step 1.

source.place: First paragraph: construct the Frobenius-equivariant truncation exact couple (E starts at page 2).

proof.text: The shift comparison in [lem-zl-field-shriek-lower-bound] gives $E_2^{a,b}=E^{a,b}\simeq\mathcal H^a(T\mathcal H^b(K))=R^ag_!(R^bh_!\mathcal F)$, an isomorphism of Weil sheaves by [lem-zl-weil-shriek-shift-compatibility]. If $b<0$ then $K_b=0$ and $\mathcal H^b(K)=0$, so $D^{a,b}=E_2^{a,b}=0$. If $a<0$ then $T\mathcal H^b(K)$ has zero cohomology in degree $a$, by preservation of the lower bound zero. Consequently $D^{a,b}=0$ for $b<0$ and $E_2^{a,b}=0$ outside the first quadrant. The derived-couple theorem [lem-sp-derived-couple-exact](4) now supplies every later page in the same abelian Weil heart, with $d_r$ of bidegree $(r,1-r)$ and $E_{r+1}=\ker d_r/\operatorname{im}d_r$.

source.place: First paragraph: identify the E_2 page and verify the first-quadrant hypotheses.

proof.text: Apply [thm-sp-half-plane-convergence] with lower bound zero to this exact couple. For each $n\ge0$ it supplies a finite decreasing filtration of $A^n=D^{0,n}=\mathcal H^n(T\tau^{\le n}K)$ whose graded pieces are $E_\infty^{a,b}$, $a+b=n$, $0\le a,b\le n$; the filtration is top for $a\le0$ and zero for $a\ge n+1$, because its defining image then comes from $D^{a,n-a}=0$. Each diagonal entry has stabilized by $r=n+2$. To identify the actual abutment, the triangle $\tau^{\le n}K\to K\to\tau^{\ge n+1}K\to$ and [lem-zl-field-shriek-lower-bound] show that $T\tau^{\ge n+1}K$ has no cohomology below $n+1$. The long exact sequence of [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles](5) therefore makes $c_n:\mathcal H^n(T\tau^{\le n}K)\to\mathcal H^n(TK)$ an isomorphism: the adjacent degree $n-1$ and $n$ cohomology groups of the third term are zero. Transport the filtration through this canonical Weil isomorphism.

source.place: First paragraph: convergence and the finite filtration of the actual abutment.

proof.text: Use the initial-page cycle and boundary subobjects in [def-sp-convergence]: $E_r^{a,b}=Z_r^{a,b}/B_r^{a,b}$, with $Z_r^{a,b}\hookrightarrow E_2^{a,b}$. These objects are formed by finitely many kernels, images and inverse images in the abelian Weil heart of step 1. At $r=n+2$, convergence in [thm-sp-half-plane-convergence] identifies this quotient with $E_\infty^{a,b}$ for every $a+b=n$. Hence put $S^{a,b}=Z_{n+2}^{a,b}$. Its subobject inclusion into $E_2^{a,b}$ is a monomorphism of constructible Weil sheaves, and the quotient projection $S^{a,b}\twoheadrightarrow E_\infty^{a,b}$ is an epimorphism of them. This gives a single subobject of the initial page, rather than merely an iterated assertion about successive subquotients.

source.place: Second paragraph: limiting terms are quotients of subobjects of E_2.

proof.text: The natural composition isomorphism of [lem-zl-field-shriek-composition-qcqs] applies to the geometric fibers of $h,g$ with the quasi-separated finite-type hypotheses checked in step 2. Its composition comparison is Frobenius-equivariant by the composition-comparison clause of [lem-fix-weil-operations]. It therefore identifies $\mathcal H^n(TK)$ with $R^n(gh)_!\mathcal F$ as Weil sheaves. Transport the decreasing filtration $F^a$ of step 5 through this isomorphism and set $m=n+1$, $G_j=F^{n+1-j}$ for $0\le j\le n+1$. Then $G_0=0$, $G_m=R^n(gh)_!\mathcal F$, and $G_j/G_{j-1}\simeq E_\infty^{n+1-j,j-1}$. For $1\le j\le m$ take $a_j=n+1-j$, $b_j=j-1$ and $S_j=S^{a_j,b_j}$ from step 6. The inclusion and quotient projection there, followed by this graded-piece isomorphism, are exactly the required monomorphism and epimorphism. Both indices are nonnegative and sum to $n$. Every object and map was constructed in the Weil heart. No weight or mixedness condition entered the argument.
